title: Order history
context: Order history screen in the app: filter by ticker, sort by a column the user picks, 50 rows per page. Active traders have hundreds of thousands of orders. Runs on PostgreSQL.

points.title: SQL injection through the ticker
points.why: The ticker is pasted into the SQL, so a value like x' OR '1'='1 returns other users' orders.
points.fix: Use bind parameters (? placeholders or NamedParameterJdbcTemplate).

points.title: ORDER BY column is injectable too
points.why: Column names can't be bound as parameters, so the sort value from the client goes into the SQL as is.
points.fix: Map the client's value to a fixed allowlist of columns and directions.

points.title: Price read as a double
points.why: Reading a NUMERIC price as a double loses precision.

points.title: OFFSET pagination on a large table
points.why: OFFSET makes the database read and discard every earlier row, so deep pages get slower and slower. New orders also shift rows between pages, so users see duplicates or gaps.
points.fix: Use keyset pagination: WHERE (created_at, id) < (:lastCreatedAt, :lastId) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 50.

points.title: Query needs a matching index
points.why: Filtering by user and ticker and sorting by date without a matching index means a scan and sort on every request.
points.fix: Add a composite index such as (user_id, ticker, created_at) in a migration.

points.title: Timestamps converted with the server's time zone
points.why: toLocalDateTime uses the JVM's default zone, so the same order shows different times on servers in different zones, and the zone is lost.
points.fix: Store timestamptz and read it as Instant or OffsetDateTime (rs.getObject("created_at", OffsetDateTime.class)); convert to the user's zone in the client.

points.title: SELECT *
points.why: Fetches columns the screen doesn't use and breaks silently when columns are added or renamed.
